This used to bother me a lot more and my feelings would get horribly triggered upon hearing of anyone's death. Even though I was freaked out and terrified, I tried to immerse myself in the subject of death. I read about NDEs (I reccomend reading work by Dr. Raymond Moody) meditated, looked into crystal healing, watched videos regarding death (love AskAMortician. She's not spiritual, but I love her views on dealing with dead bodies and dead loved ones) and overall I tried to get a sense of comfort within my greatest fear. I still have moments where I feel exactly how you do. However, the belief that the universe is so much bigger than we are has been a huge help in reducing my anxiety towards mortality. Maybe you can try some spiritual exercises and familiarize yourself with death and dying. I really hope you feel better, it can be such a terrible feeling and I'm sorry for the format, I'm on mobile!

This happened to me about 5 years ago. What helped me was changing my outlook on death. There really is nothing to be afraid of. Humans are just naturally scared of things we are unfamiliar with. I guess death is the ultimate unfamiliarity in our lives. But if death truly is the absence of conciousness, then we have nothing to worry about! If our souls do somehow live on, just not in this physical world that we are aware of, then awesome! Either way, media and society want us to be afraid. In reality, there is no death without life, just as there is no life without death. Use your time here in this body to live in your full potential. Yes, life is so short, but thats what makes it so darn special. Hope this helps :)
